messages:
incident-bot: Pager: elevated 5xx rate detected for customer AuroraComm on dedicated cluster dc-west-2-a. metric: gateway.5xx_rate > 12% for 5m. paging oncall-jamie :rotating_light:
oncall-jamie: I'm on it. booting up dashboards.
maya: Thanks — seeing a spike in 502/504 from gateway-proxy in dc-west-2-a around 15:42 UTC. Up from ~1% to ~18% in 10m.
kevin: I'm seeing a lot of backend-timeout traces during the same window, most point at model-shard-7 with high KV evictions. logs: `kv_cache_eviction: true` repeated.
sylvia: Is this single-tenant (AuroraComm) traffic or multi-tenant noisy neighbor? quick check on tenant headers?
alex: quick grep on router logs shows majority requests tagged tenant=auroracomm, but ~22% from tenant=pegasus-pub which had a huge burst at 15:40.
oncall-jamie: So mixed. Could be noisy neighbor causing shared resource pressure on dc-west-2-a. Start mitigation: route pegasus to spare pool if possible. Can eng-runtime-bot try a reroute command?
eng-runtime-bot: Running policy route command: `redwoodctl route set --tenant pegasus-pub --pool spare-west-2 --drain --timeout 30s`
Result: queued, will start draining connections in ~20s.
cs-liaison: Heads up — AuroraComm is on support tier Gold. CS is drafting a short message to notify them of partial degradation, ETA to restore ~20-30m. Let me know if we need to escalate to dedicated capacity increase.
maya: Meanwhile, adding temporary per-tenant concurrency limit for dc-west-2-a: `redwoodctl quota set --tenant pegasus-pub --concurrency 8 --cluster dc-west-2-a`
Applied.
kevin: After routing pegasus off, KV evictions decreased by ~60% in the first 2 mins. 5xx dropped from 18% to ~9% but still elevated vs baseline.
sylvia: Any evidence of GPU or host-level saturation? `nvidia-smi` and host load?
alex: Host metrics: CPU ok, GPU util ~65%. But pod-level inflight queue for AuroraComm model-shard-7 is spiking — looks like queue backlog and request queuing at the runtime layer. Also seeing OOM-kernel messages for a caching sidecar occasionally.
oncall-jamie: Could be cache thrash + hotspot on shard-7. Options: 1) temporarily shift AuroraComm traffic to model-variant with lower KV pressure, 2) reduce max tokens / request concurrency for auroracomm, 3) scale dedicated pool (takes longer).
maya: I can push a canary to route 25% of auroracomm requests to model-variant ‘gptx-small-cached’ which uses prefix-cache-friendly path. Exec: `redwoodctl rollout set --tenant auroracomm --model gptx-small-cached --pct 25 --cluster dc-west-2-a`
Result: started.
kevin: After switching 25%, 5xx for auroracomm requests at the routed subset are ~2% and end-to-end latency down 40% — good sign.
sylvia: Need to also adjust gateway timeouts to reduce downstream cascading: `gateway.conf: client_header_timeout=15s -> 10s` ? any objections? shorter timeouts may cause client visible errors but avoid long hangs.
alex: I'd rather set a soft timeout / circuit-breaker: `gatewayctl set-cb --cluster dc-west-2-a --resp-time 8s --consec-fail 5`
oncall-jamie: Do it. Apply circuit-breaker to shard-7 route only.
eng-runtime-bot: Applied circuit breaker to route shard-7. watch metrics for next 5m.
kevin: Circuit breaker tripped briefly for some requests and served 429 for a few minutes while model variant rollout continued — 5xx fell to ~3.5% overall.
cs-liaison: CS drafted external note: "We’re observing partial degradation impacting some requests to AuroraComm in dc-west-2-a. We’ve applied routing mitigations and expect reduced errors. Will follow up with root cause." Want to send now?<cs-liaison reacts: :thumbsup:>
maya: Agree send; include that we routed pegasus and rolled out model-variant canary; next update in 15m.
oncall-jamie: Observability action items: create incident ticket, attach relevant traces, and page infra SRE if 5xx >5% persists after 15m. I'll open ticket now.
incident-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-3228. Assigned to oncall-jamie. severity: P2. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-3228
kevin: I'm going to run a deeper heap/profile on shard-7 to check cache churn. `gdb` not needed, I’ll enable extended debug logging at trace level for 10m.
sylvia: Also add a KV eviction metric to the customer-facing telemetry so CS can see the pattern later — it will help the postmortem.
alex: For longer-term: recommend rebalancing hot tenants across different model-shard placements and capacity planning for AuroraComm growth. I'll start a doc.
oncall-jamie: Status: 5xx down to 2.8% after 18m from mitigation. Canary now at 35% with continued positive signal.
cs-liaison: CS updated customer message: "Errors have dropped substantially after routing changes and we continue to monitor. We will provide a root cause update after a full investigation." Sent.
kevin: Logs show remaining 5xx are mostly 504s from gateway timeouts to shard-7 under peak bursts. Looks like we need longer-term fix for shard hotspot.
maya: Marking temporary mitigations: pegasus rerouted, quota set, canary rollout. Adding an incident-runbook checklist to the ticket.
oncall-jamie: Next steps: 1) schedule shard rebalancing during off-peak (ops + infra), 2) consider autoscale policy tweak for dc-west-2-a to increase burst capacity, 3) postmortem in 48h. Anyone object?
sylvia: +1
alex: +1, I'll take rebalancing docs.
cs-liaison: We'll coordinate customer follow-up and share planned timeline for durable fix.
oncall-jamie: Closing realtime handoff — if 5xx creeps back above 5% I'll re-open page and ping infra-sre. Thanks all. :tada:
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-3228 updated: status -> monitoring, last_action_by -> oncall-jamie."
